title: Friends & Connections
description: From your course: words and phrases for making friends, getting on with people, falling out and talking about family.

items.definition: to become close to someone because you share an interest or experience
items.example: My new colleague and I [bonded over] our hatred of Monday morning meetings.
items.exampleRu: Мы с новой коллегой сблизились на почве общей ненависти к утренним планёркам по понедельникам.
items.pattern: bond over sth / bond with sb
items.trap: Use 'over' for the shared thing and 'with' for the person: 'bond with sb over sth', not 'bond on' or 'bond about'.

items.definition: to like someone and get on well with them immediately
items.example: I [clicked with] my personal trainer from the very first session.
items.exampleRu: Мы с моим персональным тренером нашли общий язык с первой же тренировки.
items.trap: Informal, and often used with no object: 'We just clicked.' Don't say 'find a common language' (from «найти общий язык»).

items.definition: to tell someone your secrets or private worries because you trust them
items.example: I don't usually [confide in] colleagues, but she's become a real friend.
items.exampleRu: Обычно я не откровенничаю с коллегами, но она стала мне настоящей подругой.
items.pattern: confide in sb (about sth) / confide sth to sb
items.trap: Use 'in' with the person: 'confide in a friend'; 'to' is only for the secret itself: 'confide a secret to sb'.

items.definition: to both know the same friend
items.example: We got chatting at the gym and realised we [had a mutual friend].
items.exampleRu: Мы разговорились в спортзале и выяснили, что у нас есть общий друг.
items.pattern: have a mutual friend / have friends in common
items.trap: Natives say 'a mutual friend' or 'a friend in common'; 'a common friend' (from «общий друг») sounds odd.

items.definition: to like each other and become friendly as soon as you meet
items.example: At my birthday party, my best friend and my cousin [hit it off] straight away.
items.exampleRu: У меня на дне рождения лучший друг и двоюродный брат сразу же подружились.
collocations: get on like a house on fire
items.trap: The 'it' is fixed: 'they hit it off', not 'they hit off'. The past form is also 'hit'.

items.definition: to think in a similar way and understand each other easily
items.example: Luckily, my new manager and I [are on the same wavelength] about most things.
items.exampleRu: К счастью, мы с новым руководителем почти во всём на одной волне.
items.pattern: be on the same wavelength (as sb)
items.trap: Use 'on' and 'wavelength': 'on the same wavelength', not 'on one wave' (from «на одной волне»).

items.definition: to go out to parties or clubs and have fun with someone
items.example: At uni I used to [party with] my friends every weekend; now I'm asleep by eleven.
items.exampleRu: В универе мы с друзьями тусили каждые выходные, а теперь я в одиннадцать уже сплю.
items.trap: As a verb, 'party' means going out drinking and dancing; for just spending time together, say 'hang out with sb'.

items.definition: to spend free time with people in a friendly way
items.example: Outside the office, I don't really [socialise with] people from work.
items.exampleRu: Вне офиса я особо не общаюсь с коллегами.
items.trap: It means spending free time together, not «общаться» as in talking or messaging (for that, say 'talk to' or 'be in touch with'). US spelling: socialize.

items.translation: близкий по взглядам; like-minded people — единомышленники
items.definition: having similar interests, ideas or opinions
items.example: A running club is a great way to meet [like-minded] people in a new city.
items.exampleRu: Беговой клуб — отличный способ найти единомышленников в новом городе.
items.trap: It's an adjective, not a noun: «единомышленники» = 'like-minded people', never just 'like-mindeds'.

items.definition: a person you work with
items.example: Could you ask one of your [colleagues] to send me the report by Friday?
items.exampleRu: Можешь попросить кого-нибудь из коллег прислать мне отчёт до пятницы?
items.trap: Stress the first syllable, ˈkɒliːɡ, not the second as in Russian «коллега»; spelt with '-league'.

items.definition: the brother of your husband or wife, or the husband of your sister
items.example: On Sunday my [brother-in-law] is coming round to help me fix the boiler.
items.exampleRu: В воскресенье ко мне зайдёт зять — поможет починить котёл.
items.trap: The plural is 'brothers-in-law'. Don't confuse it with 'son-in-law' (зять = your daughter's husband).

items.definition: the son of your brother or sister
items.example: This Saturday I'm taking my [nephew] to the Natural History Museum — he loves dinosaurs.
items.exampleRu: В эту субботу веду племянника в Музей естествознания — он обожает динозавров.
items.trap: A nephew is always a boy or man; a girl is your 'niece' (племянница).

items.definition: the way two people or groups feel about and behave towards each other
items.example: Since I moved out, my [relationship] with my dad has got so much better.
items.exampleRu: С тех пор как я живу отдельно, отношения с папой стали намного лучше.
items.pattern: a relationship with sb / between A and B
items.trap: «Отношения» with one person is singular: 'my relationship with my dad'; 'relations' is mostly for countries or groups.

items.definition: to stop being friendly with someone after an argument
items.example: I [fell out with] my best friend over a stupid argument about money.
items.exampleRu: Я разругался с лучшим другом из-за глупого спора о деньгах.
items.pattern: fall out with sb over sth
items.trap: It means the friendship is damaged, not just a short argument.

items.definition: to become friendly with someone again after an argument
items.example: They had a big fight but [made up] the next day.
items.exampleRu: Они сильно поссорились, но на следующий день помирились.
items.trap: It has many other meanings (invent, form, cosmetics); in this sense it takes no direct object: 'make up with sb'.

items.definition: to meet someone you know by chance; also, to hit someone or something by accident
items.example: We kept [bumping into] each other at the gym, so we finally went for a coffee.
items.exampleRu: Мы постоянно сталкивались в спортзале, так что в итоге сходили выпить кофе.
items.trap: Use 'into', not 'on' or 'with'. Informal; 'run into sb' means the same.

items.translation: спорить о чём-то, ругаться из-за чего-то
items.definition: to disagree with someone, often angrily, about something
items.example: Honestly, my flatmates and I [argue about] the washing-up more than anything else.
items.exampleRu: Если честно, больше всего мы с соседями по квартире спорим из-за мытья посуды.
items.trap: Use 'about' or 'over' for the topic and 'with' for the person; not 'argue on'.

items.definition: to last or continue longer than someone or something
items.example: Our friendship has [outlasted] three jobs, two moves and one terrible haircut.
items.exampleRu: Наша дружба пережила три работы, два переезда и одну ужасную стрижку.
items.trap: When a person lives longer than someone, use 'outlive' (пережить кого-то); 'outlast' is mostly about things lasting longer.

items.definition: a period of ten years
items.example: Prices in this neighbourhood have doubled over the last [decade].
items.exampleRu: За последние десять лет цены в этом районе выросли вдвое.
items.trap: Not «декада» in the sense of ten days — a decade is always ten years.

items.definition: a lot of something; many (a dozen is twelve)
items.example: I've got [dozens of] unread messages in the family chat after one evening offline.
items.exampleRu: Стоило один вечер не заходить в сеть — и в семейном чате десятки непрочитанных сообщений.
items.pattern: dozens of + plural noun / two dozen + plural noun (no 'of')
items.trap: Say 'dozens of messages', but after a number there's no -s and no 'of': 'two dozen messages'.

items.definition: a small electronic machine you carry, like a phone or tablet
items.example: You can join the call from any [mobile device], so you don't need your laptop.
items.exampleRu: К звонку можно подключиться с любого мобильного устройства, так что ноутбук не нужен.
items.trap: Sounds technical; in conversation people just say 'phone' or 'tablet'. In British English 'mobile' alone means a mobile phone.
